data.title: Fiji village restores dying fishery with coral planting
data.description: NAIDIRI - It had been decades since sharks last patrolled the reef off the coast of Fiji’s Naidiri Village, but they returned this year following a community-led effort to protect the fishery and plant thousands of corals.

data.title: Japan reports record number of foreign residents
data.description: TOKYO - Japan has registered a record number of foreigners living in the country this year despite growing anti-immigration sentiment, as the country grapples with problems caused by an ageing and shrinking population.

data.title: North Korea reports test of AI-assisted torpedo system
data.description: SEOUL - North Korea has tested a “new-type” precision-guided torpedo system that uses artificial intelligence for target detection and guidance, state media reported on Saturday, as the nuclear-armed country steps up weapons testing.

data.title: UN climate panel fails to agree date for global warming update
data.description: PARIS - The UN's IPCC climate panel failed after a week of tough talks to reach an agreement on when to release its next report on global warming, the senior French envoy at the talks said Friday.

data.title: UN climate panel fails to agree date for global warming update: envoy
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - The UN's IPCC climate panel failed after a week of tough talks to reach an agreement on when to release its next report on global warming, the senior French envoy at the talks said Friday.

data.title: Bend grieves after mass shooting: 'Who would do this to little kids?'
data.description: BEND (UNITED STATES) - Kristen Vanetsky and her family moved to Bend, Oregon, after a shooting in their New Mexico neighborhood, choosing Silver Rail elementary for her grandson because they considered it safer.

data.title: 'Great hero' praised for saving lives in Oregon school shooting
data.description: BEND (UNITED STATES) - The "hero" who shot dead a teenage gunman after he had already killed three children and a teacher at an elementary school in the US state of Oregon was named Friday by his brother.

data.title: Macron calls for calm amid fears of violence at France protests
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - President Emmanuel Macron called for calm on the eve of nationwide cost-of-living protests Saturday that authorities fear could lead to a violent escalation of weeks of student demonstrations.

data.title: Clashes grip Tirana as Albanian PM blames 'foreign hands'
data.description: TIRANA (ALBANIA) - Protesters clashed with police in Albania’s capital for the fourth day Friday as Prime Minister Edi Rama blamed "foreign hands" for mounting unrest.

data.title: EU backs Ukraine on Starlink, but can't fill gap
data.description: BRUSSELS (BELGIUM) - The European Union has pledged to help Ukraine with its dependence on Starlink satellite communications to support battlefield operations, but the bloc is a long way from being able to match the US-owned system.

data.title: US budget deficit grows to nearly $2 trillion, highest since 2021
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - The US budget deficit grew to almost $2 trillion over the past year, government data showed Friday, reaching its highest level since 2021 despite President Donald Trump's promises to cut public spending.

data.title: Trump says armed bystander who killed US school shooter a 'great hero'
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - US President Donald Trump on Friday praised the armed bystander who shot dead a teenage gunman at an Oregon elementary school as a "great hero," saying the situation could have been "much worse."

data.title: All contenders for UN chief receive veto: diplomat
data.description: UNITED NATIONS (UNITED STATES) - All seven candidates to lead the United Nations received a vote of "discourage," effectively a veto, from a permanent UN Security Council member in the latest informal poll, a diplomat said Friday.

data.title: India detains top ‘cockroach’ leader again
data.description: NEW DELHI - Indian police detained Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Abhijeet Dipke on Friday ahead of fresh protests demanding the removal of the country’s election chief, the youth-led movement said in a social media post.

data.title: Octopus populations soar in warming UK waters
data.description: LONDON - A surge in octopus numbers in British waters due to unusually warm seas is presenting fishermen with an interesting new catch — albeit one that is devouring one of their usual staples.

data.title: UN says food crisis ‘looming’ after global energy shock
data.description: Rising energy and fertiliser costs are hitting smallholder farmers and driving up prices of agricultural commodities, fuelling fears of a global food crisis, according to the head of the UN agriculture development fund.

data.title: Pope celebrates mass in hospital after cancer surgery
data.description: VATICAN CITY - Pope Leo XIV celebrated mass on Friday at the hospital where he is recovering from a lung cancer operation, as seen in the first images of him released by the Vatican since the procedure.

data.title: Italy braces for ‘autumn of discontent’
data.description: MILAN - Italy is preparing for a turbulent autumn following a spike in inflation because of energy prices, with students, truck drivers and farmers taking to the streets ahead of elections next year.

data.title: Elon Musk unveils Tesla’s ‘flying’ car
data.description: HOUSTON - Tesla CEO Elon Musk unveiled what he described as a "flying" car, equipped with thrusters, during a livestreamed event at his SpaceX rocket company on Thursday.

data.title: Cost-of-living protests to grip pre-election France
data.description: PARIS - After weeks of student protests, France is set to be swept by broader, nationwide demonstrations Saturday over the cost of living, setting up a potentially fraught period ahead of presidential elections next year.

data.title: France’s education divide laid bare by protests
data.description: BAGNOLET, France - Students cheered as they stacked rubbish bins against the entrance to a school outside Paris, while a speaker thumped out French rap to young people, teachers and parents mingling in the early morning drizzle.

data.title: Thai farmers, fishermen challenge IMF, World Bank at Bangkok rally
data.description: BANGKOK (THAILAND) - Thai farmers, fishermen and workers marched through Bangkok Friday as global finance and business leaders gathered for IMF and World Bank meetings, demanding a say in policies shaping their livelihoods.

data.title: Why India's voter revision drive has stoked fear and anger
data.description: NEW DELHI (INDIA) - India's sweeping overhaul of electoral rolls has triggered a political firestorm, with opposition parties accusing the Election Commission of putting millions at risk of disenfranchisement.

data.title: Families of children killed in Pakistan school roof collapse demand justice
data.description: PESHAWAR (PAKISTAN) - The families of children killed in a roof collapse at a school in northwest Pakistan called for "justice" on Friday, a day after more than 30 pupils and a teacher were crushed to death.

data.title: In Malaysia, frustration grows over Indonesia haze
data.description: KUALA LUMPUR - Closed schools, shuttered sports centres and mass mask handouts. Indonesian wildfire haze has caused a regional pollution crisis and prompted growing frustration in neighbours, including Malaysia.

data.title: Asian stocks rise as tech bounces from rout, Fed boss upbeat on AI
data.description: HONG KONG - Most Asian markets bounced Friday after the previous day's tech rout fuelled by concerns over the AI boom, which Federal Reserve boss Kevin Warsh said offered huge benefits to the global economy.

data.title: Trump's new press secretary says China lacked 'proper' toilets
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia, who was appointed less than a week ago, said China lacked "proper toilets" in an interview that aired on Thursday.

data.title: India closes down New Delhi park ahead of 'cockroach' movement rally
data.description: NEW DELHI (INDIA) - Authorities closed a central New Delhi park Friday before a fresh protest seeking the removal of India's election chief over a voter-roll revision that critics say has disenfranchised millions.
